saints.name: St. Hilary of Poitiers
saints.title: Bishop and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The great Western opponent of Arianism, called the Hammer of the Arians for his defense of Christ's divinity…
biography: Born about 310 at Poitiers of pagan parents of rank, Hilary came to the faith by his own study of the Scriptures and was baptized together with his wife and their daughter Abra. Chosen bishop of his city about 353, he soon stood as the foremost Western defender of the Nicene faith against Arianism.

At the synod of Béziers in 356 the emperor Constantius II banished him to Phrygia. In nearly four years of exile he mastered Greek theology and wrote the De synodis and the twelve books On the Trinity, the first full statement of the Nicene faith in Latin. Restored to his see about 361, he fought on, impeaching Auxentius, the Arian bishop of Milan, before the emperor Valentinian in 364.

With his encouragement Martin of Tours founded the monastery of Ligugé, and Jerome counts him the first Latin hymn-writer. Hilary died at Poitiers about 367; Augustine called him the illustrious doctor of the churches, and Pius IX named him Doctor of the Church in 1851. Later ages called him the Hammer of the Arians, and the Hilary term of the English courts still keeps his feast.
saints.knownFor: His defense of the divinity of Christ in the West.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Doctor of the Church (1851)
